messages.text: Your bill is ready: R$1,000. Due Friday
Only R$150? That's easy this month
The rest moves to the rotativo

steps.title: rotativo
steps.body: When you pay less than the full card bill, the rest rolls into the next month: [[revolving-credit]]. In Brazil its interest has often been above 10% a month. Since 2024 the law caps interest and fees at the size of the original debt. Simplified from real data.

steps.prompt: How does Rafa handle the R$1,000 bill? Pick one and see what's left to pay over a year.

choices.label: Pay it all now
choices.ending: Done in one month, nothing extra paid. It meant skipping a concert and cooking at home for a few weeks.

choices.label: Pay the minimum every month
choices.ending: After a year Rafa has paid about R$1,560 and still owes R$554. The interest on what's left almost eats each payment.

choices.label: Switch to a 12-month payment plan
choices.ending: R$113 a month at about 5% a month. The debt is gone in a year, and he paid about R$1,350 for a R$1,000 bill.

steps.prompt: Rafa pays the minimum for a year. Why is most of the bill still there?
options: Interest is added to what's left each month, so most of each payment covers interest
The minimum payment is a fee, not a repayment
The card adds new purchases automatically
steps.explanation: At about 12% a month, the interest on R$1,000 is R$120. A R$150 payment barely gets past it: interest on interest, working against you.

steps.prompt: Which works the same way as compound growth on savings, but against you?
steps.explanation: [[compound-interest]] grows savings on top of earlier growth. Rolled-over debt grows on top of earlier interest, the same maths in reverse.

messages.text: Your bill: R$1,000. Pay by Friday
You must pay at least R$150
The rest goes to next month, with interest

t1.body: If you don't pay the full card bill, the rest moves to next month. This is [[revolving-credit]]. In Brazil the interest has often been more than 10% every month. Since 2024, interest and fees can't be more than the debt itself.

sc1.prompt: What does Rafa do with the R$1,000 bill? Choose, then see how much he still owes during the year.

choices.label: Pay everything now
choices.ending: Done. No extra cost. He stayed home for a few weeks.

choices.label: Pay the smallest amount every month
choices.ending: After a year he paid about R$1,560 and still owes R$554. Most of the money went to interest.

choices.label: Pay in 12 equal parts
choices.ending: R$113 every month. After a year the debt is gone. He paid about R$1,350 in total.

q1.prompt: Rafa pays the smallest amount for a year. Why does he still owe so much?
options: Every month interest is added, so most of his payment pays interest
The smallest payment is a fee
The card buys new things by itself
q1.explanation: 12% of R$1,000 is R$120 in one month. He pays R$150. Only R$30 makes the debt smaller.

q2.prompt: What grows like savings with interest, but against you?
q2.explanation: Savings grow on top of earlier growth. Card debt grows on top of earlier interest. Same maths, other direction. This is [[compound-interest]].
